A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RepoGraph research. Their main text, figures, tables and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison despite v2's reformatting and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original RepoGraph experiments on SWE-bench-Lite and CrossCodeEval, together with localization, graph-variant, action-use and error analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Deepseek-Coder and Claude evaluations and a localization breakdown for successful and failed cases.

M1.justification: The parsing, relation filtering, definition/reference graph, ego-graph retrieval and procedural/agent integration procedures remain unchanged. Appendix B.2's new diagrams explain existing components; testing additional backbone models does not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate SWE-bench-Lite issue resolution and Python cross-file completion on CrossCodeEval. v2 adds no evaluated language, domain or task. The larger CrossCodeEval sample and additional backbone models change experimental settings within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds unaugmented Deepseek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct as a CrossCodeEval comparator alongside GPT-4o, with corresponding RepoGraph results. The SWE-bench comparator frameworks remain RAG, Agentless, AutoCodeRover and SWE-agent; Table 6 evaluates retained frameworks with Claude.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 changes the reported CrossCodeEval evaluation from 500 randomly selected Python samples to 2,665 Python samples. v2 also adds Deepseek-Coder evaluation and Claude-3.5-Sonnet configurations for Agentless and SWE-agent. These substantially expand the evaluation settings, while existing metrics and main GPT-based SWE-bench settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.2 and Table 7 examine whether localization accuracy differs between successful and failed Agentless+RepoGraph patches; line-level accuracy is 65.2% versus 24.6%. Existing hop/summarization ablations, action distributions, repository/year analyses and three error case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. Both use point estimates and descriptive averages; the new result rows do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 5 replaces the GPT-4o results under the enlarged reported sample: Code Match EM without/with RepoGraph changes from 10.8/28.5 to 10.5/28.7, and Deepseek-Coder adds 10.2/19.7. These are not same-setting performance changes. New Table 6 reports Claude resolve rates of 27.67/30.33 for Agentless and 23.00/25.33 for SWE-agent; Table 7 adds localization breakdowns. Table 2 revises SWE-agent token averages from 245,008/262,512 to 498,346/518,792 and baseline cost from $2.51 to $2.53. Table 3 corrects its SWE-agent file-localization gain annotation from 4.6 to 5.6.

T1.justification: The graph definitions, node categories and invocation/containment relations are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs, and v2's additional explanations introduce no new formal reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same central claims: repository-level graph context improves four software-engineering frameworks and transfers to CrossCodeEval. The stated 32.8% average relative improvement and open-source-framework state-of-the-art claim remain. The new conclusion primarily restates these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 attributes stronger CrossCodeEval gains with GPT-4o to better interpretation of retrieved context and interprets the new pass/fail analysis as supporting localization's importance. It revises the cost-benefit argument and extends the error-reduction discussion to all three categories. Appendix E's limitations remain unchanged, including its now-inconsistent GPT-4-only statement.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the Claude snapshot claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620 and identifies Deepseek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct in Table 5. Appendix B.2 adds a worked filtering illustration. Existing prompt templates, GPT snapshots, Docker setup, runtime estimates and code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds pre-LLM repository-navigation work by Begel et al. and Busjahn et al., and discusses the already-cited CodePlan's incremental dependency analysis. Other additions include Anthropic, Xiao, Ouyang and Tang references; two generic agent-application citations disappear from Appendix A.2. The main research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 adds a conclusion/discussion section, an appendix contents page and additional appendix subsections. It makes localized wording corrections and explanatory rewrites, including the ego-graph explanation and result discussions. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column formatting to a predominantly single-column ICLR layout, substantially reflowing figures and tables. v2 expands Table 5, adds Tables 6–7 and explanatory Figures 10–11, and redraws the retained repository/year plots with clearer labels and callouts. Existing appendix figures are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The larger reported CrossCodeEval evaluation, additional backbone comparisons and pass/fail localization analysis strengthen support for the existing claims. New diagrams and clearer plot labels improve comprehension. These benefits outweigh limited reporting inconsistencies: Section 5.3 retains old baseline EM values despite the revised Table 5, and Appendix E still claims only GPT-4 models were explored. The net gain is useful but incremental.
